subject.title: fix(models): clear stale auth cooldowns after early limit resets

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `models auth clear-cooldown <profile-id>` as the supported explicit escape hatch for early provider recovery, and must the same recovery be available through a guided Doctor or in-product Fix surface?
rationale: The implementation can be evaluated mechanically, but selecting a permanent public state-mutation contract—and deciding whether terminal-only recovery is acceptable for a fully blocked user—requires maintainer product intent.

options.title: Adopt with guided recovery
options.body: Approve the profile-scoped CLI escape hatch after inspectable live proof and require a discoverable Doctor or in-product Fix path as the user-facing recovery surface.

options.title: Use automatic recovery only
options.body: Pause or close this command and handle early resets entirely through bounded provider probes and runtime recovery policy.

options.title: Keep operator-only CLI
options.body: Approve the command as an advanced operator action without adding a guided recovery surface, explicitly accepting the terminal dependency.

recommendation.title: Adopt with guided recovery
recommendation.body: Approve the profile-scoped CLI escape hatch after inspectable live proof and require a discoverable Doctor or in-product Fix path as the user-facing recovery surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal combines major auth-profile invariant work with merger responsibility for related cooldown corrections.
